Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Rameezuddin Mohammed
Message:
feat: recurring payment mandates (UPI Autopay / e-mandate) — Phase 1 of the roadmap

Lets a wallet owner do one human-authenticated approval (through Razorpay's
checkout widget, over UPI) so their AI agent can then draw repeated,
variable-amount charges against it — capped by the same spend-limit policy
that already gates one-shot purchases — without a fresh checkout every time.

Wraps Razorpay's Tokens/Recurring-Payments API (customer + token, on-demand
charges), deliberately not the separate "Subscriptions" product (fixed
amount/interval, wrong fit for an agent deciding when and how much to
charge). Reuses the existing RazorpayHttpPort transport and its
idempotency/timeout/indeterminate-outcome discipline — no new HTTP
plumbing, just a new provider (RazorpayRecurringMandateProvider) alongside
RazorpayTestProvider.

New durable table (wallet.recurring_payment_mandates) — the first durable
persistence for any PaymentAuthorizationReference at all (previously
in-memory only). Defense-in-depth at the worker: the policy gate
(lifecycle-policy.ts) and the actual charge call (real-lifecycle.ts) each
independently re-read the mandate's current state before doing anything,
never trusting the job payload — fails closed if either the reference or
the lookup itself is missing.

Two things found and fixed/flagged along the way, not silently absorbed:
- Real security-relevant gap (flagged to the founder, not fixed here): this
  app's HTTP permission gate (http-api-kit/scope-enforcement.ts) never
  checks assurance level, only role-derived permissions — so the new
  step-up requirement on payment.mandate.manage is correctly modeled and
  tested at the authorization-package level but not yet actually enforced
  by any route in the app, mandate routes included. Pre-existing, app-wide,
  not introduced here.
- revoke() deliberately does NOT integrate with WalletRevocationService's
  CTP revocation-cascade machinery — that service requires a signing key
  and today only has an in-memory store wired into local-mcp, not a durable
  path control-plane-api can reach. Noted as real follow-up, not faked.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Kiro Agent
Message:
fix: real idempotency request fingerprint + per-tenant key namespace, route tests, provider idempotency guard

Addresses review iteration 1 (NEEDS_CHANGES) findings:

- Issue 1: runWithIdempotency now folds a stable hash of the request
  (merchant + method + route path + Idempotency-Key + canonically
  serialized body) into the sha256 digest instead of only merchantId:key.
  A changed body now yields digest_conflict (409); same body replays.
- Issue 2: the persisted natural key is namespaced per tenant + operation
  (merchantId::method::path::key) so a client-chosen key cannot collide
  across merchants on the store's single-partition row. No store SQL change.
- Issue 3: adds HTTP route-level idempotency tests (replay, changed-body
  409, in_flight, cross-tenant no-collision) using the in-memory adapter,
  no DB required.
- Issue 5: documents an explicit per-transactionId idempotency contract on
  PaymentAuthorizationPort and adds guard comments at the provider seam and
  the reconciliation-mismatch retry so a live connector cannot double-capture.

Issue 4 (agent-runtime fail-closed with no real handlers) is the intended
FEAT-001 behavior and is documented in FEAT-005.json, not 'fixed' with mocks.
